question: Pipes A and B can empty a tank in 15 hours and 18 hours, respectively. Pipe C alone can fill the tank in 6 hours. If all the three pipes are opened together, then two-third part of the tank will be full after:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total capacity of tank = LCM(15, 18, 6) = 90 units.

Efficiencies: Pipe A = −6, Pipe B = −5, Pipe C = +15 (Net efficiency = 15 − 11 = +4 units/hr).

Target work = 2/3 of total capacity = (2/3) × 90 = 60 units.

Time required = Target work ÷ Net efficiency = 60 ÷ 4 = 15 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Pipe A to empty = 15 hours

Time taken by Pipe B to empty = 18 hours

Time taken by Pipe C to fill = 6 hours

**Calculation:**

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Time (Hours)**
 **Total Work (LCM)**
 **Efficiency (Units/Hr)**
 
 

 A (Empty)
 15
 90
 −6
 
 

 B (Empty)
 18
 −5
 
 

 C (Fill)
 6
 +15
 
 

⇒ Net efficiency of (A + B + C) = (−6) + (−5) + 15

⇒ Net efficiency = 15 − 11 = 4 units/hr (Positive sign implies the tank is filling)

⇒ Target part of the tank to be filled = 2/3 of 90 units

⇒ Target work = (2 ÷ 3) × 90 = 60 units

⇒ Time required = Target work ÷ Net efficiency

⇒ Time required = 60 ÷ 4 = 15 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 15 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sign Convention for Pipes

Always assign a positive efficiency to an inlet (filling) pipe and a negative efficiency to an outlet (emptying) pipe or a leak.

Combined Rate of Filling

If pipe A fills in x hours and pipe B empties in y hours, then their net part filled in 1 hour is (1/x − 1/y). If the result is positive, the tank fills; if negative, the tank empties.

Concept of Fractional Work

Time required to complete a specific fraction of a tank = (Fraction × Total Capacity) ÷ Combined Efficiency.
